fixture: Recorded on macOS arm64 with quantproof 0.1.0 installed via pip install -e . (Python 3.12.13); outputs captured non-interactively, so rich progress bars are replaced by plain status lines. llama-server was not installed on the recording machine, so step 3 substitutes the deterministic stub server from tests/stub_llama_server.py via --server-bin: the stub stands in for the model, returning canned answers for the bundled example pack (degraded answers for low-bits-per-weight filenames like IQ2_XXS). Server spawn, /health wait, sampling over /v1/chat/completions, both graders (cc compile + diff, substring checks) and the collapse-delta table are the real code paths; the pass rates and tok/s shown demonstrate pipeline mechanics, not quant quality — tok/s is latency-derived and varies per machine. With llama-server on PATH and real GGUF files, the same rank command without --server-bin runs the real calibration. The two .demo.gguf files are 8-byte placeholders the stub never reads.
